newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil rides with crude, but business slow.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil rides with crude, but business slow.

text.p: Fuel oil was buffeted by the fall and rise in crude's fortunes on Thursday with most dealers seeing levels broadly unchanged to narrowly easier from Wednesday.
High sulphur barges came under heavy selling pressure, but cargoes were more resistant in a market that was quiet after an industry function last night and another scheduled for tonight.

High sulphur barges opened around $125 fob ARA, but fell as low as $121.50 in lacklustre physical bunker demand. One of the main sellers of the day was expecting 60,000 tonnes to come into ARA over the weekend.
Traders said cargoes were steady around $115-117 fob NWE, but were did not agree about prospects.

Some players saw a lack of demand hindering short-term gains, but other dealers said supply did not look to be matching interest. ESB's buying of 60kt of Russian straight-run over the last week supported those traders who saw this quality as well supplied and its potential bearish impact on the cracked market.

Low sulphur was looking softer at the end of the day, having lost ground with crude and at $124-126 fob NWE, a touch under swaps. Activity was slow after the $134.50 fob NWE done yesterday with the Med buyer quiet. -- London +44 171 542 8980
